scope: ExtendedString pointer SetValue defined self-overlap and Insert self-alias boundary

occt.allocation_configuration: Pinned modeling-full TKernel flags define no OCCT_MMGT_OPT_* allocator override; Standard::Reallocate therefore uses the source default realloc path.

source_behavior.SetValue: The pointer wrapper computes extStringLen before calling SetValue(where,pointer,length). The implementation does not reallocate when where-1+length <= myLength and copies one unit at a time in increasing index order, so self-overlap can change later source reads.
source_behavior.Insert: The pointer wrapper computes extStringLen and delegates to the explicit-length overload. That implementation calls reallocate(myLength+length) before reading/copying the source pointer; same-object alias input is not a defined behavior contract after reallocation.
source_behavior.Standard::Reallocate: The pinned build uses Standard::Reallocate default branch backed by realloc; successful reallocation invalidates old pointer values, so no native self-alias output is asserted for Insert or growing SetValue.

declarations.scope_note: The bounded-slice adapter covers null and external-pointer paths. The offset adapter reproduces non-growing self-pointer calls, including forward-overlap effects. A self-pointer write that would extend Length is rejected as Standard_NotImplemented because native SetValue reallocates before reading that pointer; this is a native undefined domain, not claimed behavior.

The bounded-slice adapter covers the null and external-pointer paths. Self-pointer calls are excluded: native Insert reallocates before reading the pointer, which invalidates a same-object source under the pinned allocator contract.

observations: Self SetValue writes target-after-source overlap in increasing index order; earlier writes are subsequently observed as source units.
Self SetValue target-before-source overlap copies the original suffix without altering later source values.
A pointer at the receiver terminator is an empty input and leaves the string unchanged when index is valid.
An empty source pointer still reaches native index validation first and invalid index 0 raises Standard_OutOfRange with the pinned message.
No output was collected for self-alias Insert or growing self-alias SetValue because the native source reallocates before using the old pointer.

limitations: Insert same-object self aliasing is excluded because the native implementation reallocates before reading its source pointer; no output from an invalidated pointer is used as an oracle.

The self SetValue offset API accepts source offsets in the current logical code-unit storage, including the terminator, and refuses an operation that would extend the old Length. External pointer buffers remain modeled by Option<&[u16]>.
The Rust NotImplemented error for a growing self-alias is a safe refusal for a native undefined domain, not a reproduced OCCT exception.
